description:
# Jensen Huang Ousted: Timeline Of The Nvidia Scandal—As Board Chair Dismisses Reinstatement Push
Nov 18, 2026, 12:49pm EST

[Add Forbes on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=forbes.com)

## Topline
Nvidia’s board chair [told](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/17/nvidia-board-chair-says-jensen-huang-reinstatement-isnt-being-considered/) investors Tuesday the board is not considering reinstating ousted CEO Jensen Huang despite a public campaign to do so, as the embattled tech mogul is trying to mount a comeback amid the scandal over his multiple alleged affairs—even as he comes under increasing governmental scrutiny.

![Jensen Huang leather jacket](https://imageio.forbes.com/specials-images/imageserve/6af5ef2a43e68c8caef0362b/Jensen-Huang-leather-jacket/0x0.jpg?format=jpg&crop=1920,1080,x0,y0,safe&width=1440)

## Timeline
18Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who chairs the Senate Banking Committee, told [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/jensen-huang-nvidia-tim-scott-congress.html) that Huang has agreed to testify before the committee next month, likely at a public hearing, marking at least the second congressional appearance the ex-CEO is slated to make in the coming weeks.

17Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said on the company’s [earnings call](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/17/nvidia-board-chair-says-jensen-huang-reinstatement-isnt-being-considered/) that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” adding the board had “unanimously” accepted Huang’s resignation and had already retained a firm to help lead its search for his successor.

Nvidia’s board “acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company’s employees, customers, partners, and shareholders” in how it handled Huang’s resignation, Jones said, though Semafor [reports](https://www.semafor.com/article/11/17/2026/some-nvidia-directors-push-to-bring-huang-back-despite-board-opposition) there are a subset of board members who are still pushing for Huang to be reinstated.

17The Securities and Exchange Commission opened a probe into Nvidia in the wake of Huang’s ouster, the Wall Street Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/business/sec-is-probing-nvidia-amid-departure-of-ceo-jensen-huang-ee7643f8) citing anonymous sources, though the full scope of the investigation is still unclear.

17Huang issued his [first public statement](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2026/11/17/jensen-huang-says-hed-be-honored-to-return-as-nvidia-ceo-in-first-public-statement-since-resigning-in-scandal/) since resigning, saying he “would be honored” to return as CEO if the board asked him to.

17House lawmakers [announced](https://www.forbes.com/sites/saradorn/2026/11/17/huang-agrees-to-testify-before-congress-on-dec-1/) Huang will testify on Dec. 1 before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee; the “transcribed interview” is expected to take place behind closed doors, though a transcript could later be made public.

16Sources [cited](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/16/nvidia-board-not-weighing-huangs-return-as-ceo-01167741) by [multiple](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/silicon-valley-leaders-back-call-jensen-huangs-return-nvidia-2026-11-16/) [outlets](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang.html) indicated Nvidia’s board is so far not considering reinstating Huang as CEO, potentially dashing Huang and his allies’ hopes as the board’s approval remains essential to [any comeback effort](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2026/11/16/could-jensen-huang-return-as-nvidia-ceo-here-are-the-possible-paths/).

16Nvidia shares were sharply down in [premarket trading](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2026/11/16/nvidia-shares-slip-in-premarket-as-jensen-huang-reportedly-weighs-ceo-comeback/) Monday morning amid reports of Huang’s potential comeback, and the stock opened 2% [down](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/), with [Huang’s net worth](https://www.forbes.com/profile/jensen-huang/) dropping from $141.9 billion before market open to $138.6 billion as of 9:45 a.m. EST.

The stock continued to decline Monday, causing Huang to [fall one ranking](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/16/jensen-huang-loses-another-6-billion-on-monday-extending-his-net-worth-decline-to-16-over-the-past-week/) on Forbes’ [Real-Time Billionaires list](https://www.forbes.com/real-time-billionaires/) as he dropped to 14th richest in the world and was overtaken by Walmart heiress Alice Walton.

15The Financial Times [reported](https://www.ft.com/content/45383d86-33c4-4d99-86e5-5e058d3567c1?syn-25a6b1a6=1) Huang is considering mounting a [comeback](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2026/11/16/nvidia-shares-slip-in-premarket-as-jensen-huang-reportedly-weighs-ceo-comeback/) at Nvidia, speaking with allies about returning to the company as supporters launch a “war room” and [petition](https://standwithjensen.com/#supporters) lobbying for his return.

13Billionaire investor [Leo KuGuan](https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2026/11/13/billionaire-investor-koguan-vows-to-stop-buying-nvidia-stock-after-huang-exit-musk-and-others-back-ex-ceo/), previously a significant [investor](https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2026/03/04/billionaire-leo-koguan-just-spent-180-million-on-this-ai-stock/?ctpv=searchpage) in Nvidia, said he would stop investing in Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, telling [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-13/billionaire-koguan-vows-not-to-buy-nvidia-stock-as-huang-quits?srnd=homepage-americas) on Friday, “No further investment without Jensen,” also [saying](https://x.com/KoguanLeo/status/2121078999116112326) on X he would instead “invest more in other si companies,” using President Donald Trump’s preferred term for artificial intelligence, “super intelligence” or “SI.”

12Hours after Huang’s resignation, Reuters [reported](https://www.reuters.com/technology/former-nvidia-ceo-huang-had-relationship-with-second-employee-sources-say-2026-11-12/) the ousted CEO had a relationship with a second Nvidia employee, marking the [third affair](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2026/11/12/jensen-huang-had-a-third-affair-with-another-nvidia-employee-report-says/) Huang is alleged to have had.

12Nvidia [announced](https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2026/11/12/jensen-huang-out-at-nvidia-after-affair-scandals/) Huang’s immediate resignation as president and CEO and from the company’s board, naming Colette Kress as the interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones as chairman of the board.

Huang has not yet commented on his resignation, though the New York Times [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/12/business/nvidia-jensen-huang-resigns/5721cf82-58ca-5b51-a1b8-0f43d581ecc4?smid=url-share) Thursday afternoon he’s retained attorneys from law firm Paul Weiss.

12Huang’s net worth took a 10% dive upon market open as the [company’s stock price](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/12/nvidia-sinks-11-at-open-after-jensen-huang-resigns-pushing-market-cap-below-microsoft/) tumbled amid the news, dropping from $151 billion to $135 billion at market open.

11The New York Times [reports](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-affair.html) Huang had a second affair with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, which he has not yet confirmed—saying only, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” when reached for comment by the Times.

11Congress [ramped up](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-11/congress-set-to-subpoena-nvidia-s-jensen-huang-republican-says) its investigation into Huang and his relationship with Alice Huang, with Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who chairs the House China Committee, telling Fox Business that Huang had until the end of the day Wednesday to respond to a letter from lawmakers requesting information, or else he would be subpoenaed.

11Reports shortly after news of the second affair broke suggested Nvidia’s board was prepared to oust Huang as the company’s CEO, with the Wall Street Journal [reporting](https://www.wsj.com/business/nvidia-is-preparing-to-oust-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-30f421ad?st=yfWjq1&reflink=article_copyURL_share) the board could decide the CEO’s fate as soon as Wednesday evening.

10Huang officially [fell out](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/10/jensen-huang-is-no-longer-among-worlds-10-richest-as-nvidia-slump-continues/) of Forbes ranking of the 10 richest people in the world as Nvidia’s stock price—and his net worth by extension—sank amid the scandals, putting him [below](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/09/jensen-huang-drops-below-warren-buffett-and-larry-ellison-in-billionaire-rankings-amid-scandal/) Warren Buffett and Larry Ellison.

9Huang pulled out of speaking engagements planned for this week as scrutiny on him intensified, with TechCrunch [reporting](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/jensen-huang-pulls-out-of-elevenlabs-summit-amid-nvidia-controversy/) he cancelled planned appearances at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

Nov. 9 [Nvidia’s stock](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/09/jensen-huang-drops-below-warren-buffett-and-larry-ellison-in-billionaire-rankings-amid-scandal/) dropped 7% in premarket trading and more than 7% at market open on Monday, the first trading day after the investigation into Huang was revealed, with Huang’s net worth falling $7.4 billion in the first half-hour of trading and briefly kicking him off the list of the top 10 richest people before the stock slightly rebounded.

8Nvidia’s board [announced](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2026/11/08/nvidia-investigating-ceo-jensen-huangs-relationship-with-alleged-chinese-spy-after-he-admits-affair/) it was investigating whether Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort” after The New York Times first reported his alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen whom the U.S. government believes may be an asset to the Chinese government.

Huang confirmed the affair in a statement to employees Sunday, saying he was “unfaithful to my wife” and vowing to cooperate with the probe, telling employees he was “fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence.”

5Moolenaar and other lawmakers on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs sent a formal request to Huang for him to brief lawmakers on his relationship with Alice Huang, arguing the reports of their relationship “raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information.”

29The Times first [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html) Huang has a “close relationship” with Alice Huang, an executive at data center company Megaspeed whom U.S. officials had “concluded … was a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing.”

2025Trump was first informed that Huang had a social relationship with Alice Huang and she was believed to be a “Chinese intelligence asset,” but the Times [reports](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/business/nvidia-jensen-huang-affairs-timeline.html) the president chose not to take any further action.

Late 2024The federal government first began its investigation into Alice Huang’s company Megaspeed, with the Times [reporting](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html) the probe was transferred from the Commerce Department to the Justice Department in 2025 amid concerns Alice Huang could be helping China access more advanced AI chips and funneling intelligence to Beijing.

2023Huang was spotted with Alice Huang for the first time at a dinner with colleagues at a restaurant in Singapore; the Times [notes](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/business/nvidia-jensen-huang-affairs-timeline.html) it’s still unclear when they first met and their relationship began.

## Forbes Valuation
Forbes values [Huang’s net worth](https://www.forbes.com/profile/jensen-huang/) at $133.4 billion as of 12:45 p.m. EST on Wednesday. He remains off the list of the world’s 10 richest people, and Forbes currently [ranks him](https://www.forbes.com/real-time-billionaires/) as the 14th richest person in the world after he [dropped](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/16/jensen-huang-loses-another-6-billion-on-monday-extending-his-net-worth-decline-to-16-over-the-past-week/) further down the list on Monday. Huang’s wealth is based on a more than 3.5% stake in Nvidia, and the company did not give any indication Thursday that he will divest his shares or lose his stake in the company after resigning. He does not have voting power through his Nvidia shares, [according](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/12/business/nvidia-jensen-huang-resigns/dab33311-f07e-51db-8105-217e2aa756ba?smid=url-share) to the Times.

title: Jensen Huang breaks silence after resigning from Nvidia, says he " ...
description:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang broke his silence after [resigning](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns/) from the company following revelations of multiple affairs, saying he'd be willing to return as its CEO.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," Huang said in a statement Tuesday morning.

Late Tuesday, however, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones said the company's board doesn't intend to rehire Huang as chief executive.

## Support for Huang's return
Huang has gained support from more than 190,000 people, including several thousand Nvidia employees, who [signed a petition](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-reinstatement-petition/) to reinstate him. On Monday, President Trump suggested to reporters that he would support Huang returning to Nvidia.

Later, the president said he recommended former [Apple CEO Tim Cook](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-next-nvidia-ceo-candidates/) as Nvidia's next leader.

In his Tuesday statement, Huang thanked his allies for their support since his departure last week, saying that in addition to the public calls for him to return to the company, many "continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive and geopolitical dynamics."

Nvidia's board said on Tuesday that it has formed a committee to [oversee its national security](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-return-statement/) policies and ensure compliance with U.S. export controls. The former CEO has also agreed to appear before House lawmakers on Dec. 1 to address questions about a potential breach of national security amid an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

The former CEO's return to Nvidia is unlikely, said Yorkville Ives & Co. technology analyst Dan Ives.

"In our view the sequencing is the tell: Jensen has conditioned his return on a board decision, and the board's first public act this week was to build a compliance structure around the issue that forced him out, which is not what a board preparing to reverse itself does," he said in a Tuesday research note.

Shares of Nvidia declined $2.63, or 1.7%, to $153.51. The stock has lost 16% of its value since Huang's extramarital relationships became public.

The company's interim CEO, Colette Kress, told investors Tuesday that the company's "roadmap is on track" in the company's first earnings report since Huang's resignation.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/gettyimages-2266444753-20261117204747952.jpg?c=original&q=w_1041,c_fill)

The company's interim CEO, Colette Kress, told investors Tuesday that the company's "roadmap is on track" in the company's first earnings report since Huang's resignation.

Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night.

The announcement comes after Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO, should the board allow it. Huang [abruptly resigned last week](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/12/tech/jensen-huang-nvidia-resigns) amid national security concerns and reports of multiple extramarital affairs.

The company sought to reassure investors and offer clarity about its future in the third-quarter earnings report Tuesday evening, with Kress, saying Nvidia’s “roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.”

Nvidia releases earnings reports and says whether Jensen Huang will return as CEO

3:18

Nvidia releases earnings reports and says whether Jensen Huang will return as CEO

3:18

“Our ambition will not change, our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change,” Kress told investors, whose confidence in the company’s future [has been badly shaken by the scandal](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/13/business/nvidia-jensen-huang-affair-fallout-vis), on the earnings call.

It’s the first financial picture investors are getting since the chipmaker was shaken last week by Huang’s resignation after three decades at the helm of the company he founded.

Nvidia more than doubled its quarterly revenue and profit from a year prior, and both figures beat Wall Street’s expectations.

[![Jensen Huang looks on during a press briefing in Paris on October 13.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/c-gettyimages-2299645290.jpg?c=16x9&q=h_720,w_1280,c_fill/w_256)\

Nvidia shares were coming off their worst week in 19 months heading into the report. The stock is down 16.7% since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair and Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, erasing $751 billion in market value. Since Nvidia shares hit their record high on October 6, they have dropped 35%, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market value.

Nvidia shares have dropped for four consecutive days since Huang resigned. Shares fell just 0.44% Tuesday. But shares moved higher in after-hours trading after the earnings release and analyst call, gaining roughly 5% as of 6:10 p.m.

“The massive results, strong guidance and reassurance that the strategy Huang put in place remains firmly on track show that an orderly CEO transition does not necessarily have to dilute the company’s value,” Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com, said in emailed commentary following the release. He added that Nvidia’s growth train “can continue with or without Huang, provided the company makes the right call on leadership.”

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim leader.

From Nvidia

Some Nvidia employees, investors and other tech leaders had [called on the board](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/15/business/jensen-huang-resigned-nvidia-support) to reinstate Huang as CEO, pending the outcome of its investigation into his multiple reported extramarital affairs, including with former Megaspeed executive [Alice Huang](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/12/politics/alice-huang-us-intel-jensen-huang-nvidia), whom US officials suspect as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; and at least one direct subordinate at Nvidia.

Huang [said Tuesday](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/17/business/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-statement) that he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided that his “return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America,” in his first public comment since resigning.

Meanwhile, Huang is [set to testify](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/17/politics/live-news/trump-visit-china-philippines?post-id=cmwkvv2e100003b6to3eqbow3) on Capitol Hill on December 1. He is expected to face questions about his relationship with [Alice Huang](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/12/politics/alice-huang-us-intel-jensen-huang-nvidia) and Nvidia’s sales of chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which some [US officials believed](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/16/tech/nvidia-sex-spies-serious-problems) should have been labeled a national security risk.

Some US sources say that whether or not Alice Huang was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions.

## Another strong quarter
Huang’s exit aside, concerns about whether the [AI trade is a bubble](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/13/business/ai-stock-tech-bubble) about to burst, with valuations and infrastructure spending outpacing returns, had already begun to reach a fever pitch in recent months. Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, [told CNN this week](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/16/economy/ai-bubble-anthropic-ipo-recession) that he believes the AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election.

Nvidia’s Tuesday report indicates that, at least for now, the company’s growth continues to outpace Wall Street’s expectations.

The company posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% year-on-year. Profits reached more than $65 billion, up 105% year-on-year. Kress also said demand for the company’s next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology is “off to an explosive start,” with the tech already in use by customers such as Google, Microsoft and Oracle.

Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains strong, with a handful of the biggest AI and cloud companies [expected to](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-25/goldman-sees-hyperscaler-ai-capex-rising-50-to-1-2-trillion) shell out more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures next year alone. But in the wake of Huang’s exit, investors have been more concerned with the company’s future business.

The report also comes after a blue wave in the US midterm elections ushered in a slate of newly elected leaders, many of whom [campaigned on](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/11/tech/ai-data-center-opponents-midterm-fight) slowing or restricting data center development, which could dent Nvidia’s business.

Analysts with research firm IDC wrote in a [report last week](https://www.idc.com/resource-center/blog/nvidia-ceo-resignation-ai-infrastructure-buyers/) that the firm sees “near-term AI infrastructure demand and supply as largely locked in, so the harder questions,” like long-term bets on emerging technologies and the financing system that [Jensen Huang sat in the center of](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/17/business/jensen-huang-return-risk), “sit further out.”

Nvidia said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to come in around $130 billion, plus or minus 3% — exceeding what Wall Street analysts had predicted, according to consensus estimates from FactSet.

Kress raised the company’s growth estimates for next year even higher from its already-ambitious targets, saying Nvidia’s revenue is expected to grow by 75% in fiscal 2028, up from 70% in the last earnings call.

Shipments of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China made up less than 1% of sales in its core data center business in the [previous quarter](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2027/NVDA-2027-Q2-10Q-Final-including-exhibits.pdf). However, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15% of revenues when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.”

The Commerce Department on Monday [tightened export restrictions](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/16/politics/ai-chips-restrictions-china) designed to prevent China from accessing sensitive, AI-powering computer chips via data centers in third-party countries.

The company earned $2.4 billion in sales of licensed chips to China during the third quarter, but it has ceased such shipments, Kress said during Tuesday’s call.

Kress ended with a rallying call to Nvidia’s investors, customers and employees: “We’ve got this.”
